div.note: Heading only in H (in red), after Walreaf; Liebermann would correct to ‘gerædn.’. B has no heading, so K is empty. Base text B = CCCC 383 (c. 1130); H = Textus Roffensis; Ot = Cotton Otho B XI (burnt; here mostly known from Somner's transcript, So).; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads); Wormald, Making of English Law I, October 2026 (was “925–c.935; before III–VI As (Attenborough); Grately; c.926–c.930 (Whitelock)”, now “925–c.935 (Liebermann); before III–VI As (Attenborough); c.926–c.930 (Whitelock); not before 928 (Wormald); Grately”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “925–c.935 (Liebermann); before III–VI As (Attenborough); c.926–c.930 (Whitelock); not before 928 (Wormald); Grately”, now “925–c.935 (Liebermann, I p. 150); before III–VI As (Attenborough); c.926–c.930 (Whitelock, EHD p. 418); not before 928 (Wormald, MEL p. 440); Grately”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 150; German 151”; 60 rows of II As); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Attenborough (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “126 / 127”; 60 rows of II As)

note.seg: Die Überschrift ist nicht archetyp, da sie nur in H und Q ii vorkommt, und in ihnen nicht gleich, sondern ebenso verschieden wie die vor anderen Stücken derselben Kompilatoren lautet
The heading is not archetypal, since it occurs only in H and Q ii, and is not identical in them but differs just as the headings before other pieces by the same compilers do

Die späte Zeit H's macht möglich, die Endung -esse auch für Sing. zu halten. Ist es Plural, so meinte H entweder II As allein oder begriff vielleicht V As, das unmittelbar folgt, mit darunter. — Das -d- fehlt H auch I Ew Insc¹

The late date of H makes it possible to take the ending -esse as singular too. If it is plural, H meant either II As alone or perhaps included under it V As, which immediately follows. — H also lacks the -d- at I Ew Insc¹
